profile.summary: JanusDNA is a DNA language model that reads sequence one nucleotide at a time and is designed for long inputs. It is pre-trained on the human reference genome so that each position is predicted from the sequence on both sides of it, and its learned representations are then fine-tuned for tasks such as regulatory element classification and eQTL prediction. The models are small: the README lists sizes of 1.980M to 2.009M and 7.662M parameters.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The input sequence is encoded by two independent stacks, one reading left to right and one right to left. Each stack has 8 layers, each with a Mamba block and a feed-forward block, and half of the feed-forward blocks are replaced by mixture-of-experts blocks with 16 experts. A final fusion layer, a FlexAttention layer with 4 heads, joins the two directions with an attention mask that lets the prediction for a position see the left context from the forward pass and the right context from the backward pass, but not the position itself. This lets every token contribute to the loss, as in autoregressive training, while the model still learns from both sides, as in masked training. One variant also replaces the Mamba block in the fifth layer with a causal attention layer (mid-attention). A later update adds two MLP layers after the fusion layer.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The paper pre-trains three widths: hidden size 32 and 72 for 1,024-nucleotide inputs (10,000 steps), and 144 for 131,072-nucleotide inputs (50,000 steps). The 32 and 72 widths come with and without mid-attention. The weights dataset on Harvard Dataverse (version 2) holds five original checkpoints with their configuration files and five later checkpoints with the final MLP layers (JanusDNA_mlp), which the README calls the latest. The GenomicBenchmarks script expects a pretrained checkpoint under outputs/pretrain/hg38/, in a folder named after its configuration. A result should give the width, the input length, whether mid-attention was used and whether the final MLP was used.

sections.title: Setting up the code
sections.body: The README covers environment setup and scripts that reproduce the paper: pre-training on hg38 and fine-tuning on GenomicBenchmarks, the Nucleotide Transformer tasks and the DNALongBench eQTL tasks. Setup uses a conda environment file and a prebuilt Mamba wheel for CUDA 12, PyTorch 2.5 and Python 3.11 on Linux x86_64. The scripts contain placeholder paths to fill in, and the GenomicBenchmarks script is written for 8 GPUs. The README gives no example of loading a checkpoint and embedding a single sequence.

facts.label: Model type
facts.value: Bidirectional DNA foundation model (language model) trained with a combined autoregressive and masked objective

quotes.text: the first bidirectional DNA foundation model built upon a novel pretraining paradigm that combines the optimization efficiency of autoregressive modeling with the bidirectional comprehension of masked modeling

facts.label: Architecture
facts.value: Hybrid Mamba, attention and mixture-of-experts. Two 8-layer unidirectional encoders (Mamba plus feed-forward blocks, half replaced by 16-expert MoE blocks), joined by a FlexAttention fusion layer with 4 heads. Optional mid-attention layer at layer 5; optional final MLP layers.

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: DNA sequence, tokenised at single-nucleotide resolution.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Per-nucleotide representations that the repository's scripts fine-tune into task predictions (classification for the benchmark tasks; eQTL prediction evaluated by AUROC). The pre-training head predicts each nucleotide.

facts.label: Parameters
facts.value: The README gives model sizes of 1.980M (with mid-attention), 1.988M (without), 2.001M and 2.009M (final-MLP versions) for the configurations used on the Nucleotide Transformer tasks, and 7.662M (7.745M with the final MLP) for the DNALongBench configuration. The paper reports these as activated parameters; with all mixture-of-experts weights counted the totals are larger (paper Table 9).

strengths.text: Very small models, of about 2M to 7.7M activated parameters. The authors report results against models with 250 times more activated parameters; that is their claim.

quotes.text: Here, we specifically focus only on the architecture, and thus use only the human reference genome for pretraining to ensure a fair comparison.

limitations.text: The 1 million base pair figure is an architectural capacity. The longest released checkpoint was pre-trained at 131,072 nucleotides, and the others at 1,024.

no_run_guide_reason: The README gives environment setup and Slurm or multi-GPU scripts that reproduce pre-training and benchmark fine-tuning, with placeholder paths to fill in. It gives no command or code to load a released checkpoint and run inference, and does not say where to place the Dataverse checkpoints for its scripts. A guide would need steps the sources do not give.
notes: The README links the weights with a Dataverse URL ending version=DRAFT; the Dataverse API shows version 2 as released on 2025-09-30, and that is the version described. The Dataverse author field is a placeholder ('this, author'), but the dataset is linked from the official README. No Hugging Face release was found.
